contents.text:
I'm settling on the core decision: no product names in core, identities and packs as separate contracts, and packs never referencing other packs or identities. Hosts pick identities and packs at start-up within one composition project. I'll note the consequences, and I'm weighing whether to show the overview page, since the identity and pack places already sit there, so it may not be needed. I'll keep the answer short, offer a few choices, and cite the ADR at src/docs/adr/0027-engine-identities-and-packs.md.

I'm noting that the ADR is marked accepted and dated 2026-10-19. I also want to keep the answer in paragraphs rather than lists, since lists are for steps and choices, and use short sentences.

ADR 0027 decides that the engine names no product. Puls, the demo, the coding agent and voorman had grown into the core. The ADR splits that into three parts: an engine, identities and packs.

The engine keeps the loop, sessions, usage and prices, guards, the contracts, and the tools every identity needs. It names no product and no country.

An identity, `IAgentIdentity`, says who an agent is. That covers its voice, modes, roles and the packs it uses, by name.

A pack, `IAgentPack`, says what an agent can do. That covers toolsets, providers, guides and settings. A pack never references another pack or an identity. The ADR notes that `ArchitectureTests` enforces this.

A single composition project, `src/hosts/LouisAgent.Composition`, knows all of them. A host picks its identities and packs with the `IDENTITIES` and `PACKS` settings at start-up.

The consequence is that a new product is configured, not coded. Adding an identity or pack adds no branch to the core. Identities and packs load only at start-up, so a chat's tools never change under it.

Source: `src/docs/adr/0027-engine-identities-and-packs.md`
